metadata.subject: Chemistry
metadata.topic: Electrochemistry — Faraday's Law: Volume of H₂ at Electrolysis
metadata.note: Uses dilute aqueous sodium chloride electrolysis. Reaction at cathode: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂. F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹, molar volume at RTP = 24 dm³ mol⁻¹.

question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2024 Q4c — Electrolysis: Volume of H₂ Produced
question.text:
During the electrolysis of dilute aqueous sodium chloride using a current of 1.0 A for 30 minutes, hydrogen gas is produced at the cathode.

Calculate the volume of hydrogen produced, measured at room temperature and pressure (rtp).

Given:
F = 9.65 × 10⁴ C mol⁻¹ (Faraday constant)
Molar volume of gas at rtp = 24 dm³ mol⁻¹
Half equation at cathode: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂
question.general_feedback:
Model solution:
Step 1: Convert time → t = 30 × 60 = 1 800 s
Step 2: Calculate charge → Q = I × t = 1.0 × 1 800 = 1 800 C
Step 3: Moles of electrons → n(e⁻) = Q / F = 1 800 / 96 500 = 0.01865 mol
Step 4: Moles of H₂ → n(H₂) = n(e⁻) / 2 = 0.01865 / 2 = 0.009326 mol (from 2e⁻ per H₂)
Step 5: Volume at rtp → V = n × 24 = 0.009326 × 24 = 0.224 dm³

steps.label:
Given: I = 1.0 A  |  t = 30 min  |  F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹  |  molar volume at rtp = 24 dm³ mol⁻¹
Cathode equation: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂ (2 moles of electrons produce 1 mole of H₂)
Chain: t(s) → Q = It → mol e⁻ = Q/F → mol H₂ = mol e⁻ / 2 → V = mol H₂ × 24
Convert time and calculate charge Q. (2 marks)
Calculate moles of electrons transferred. (1 mark)
Calculate moles of H₂ and its volume at rtp. (2 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Time must be in seconds. 30 minutes × 60 s/min = 1 800 s.
Q = I × t = 1.0 × 1 800 = 1 800 C. Did you convert 30 min to seconds first?
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Charge formula: Q = I × t (current in amps × time in seconds).
Moles of electrons = total charge ÷ Faraday constant (96 500 C/mol).

fields.label: Moles of H₂ produced n(H₂) = _____ mol
fields.diagnostic_hint: From 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂: 2 mol electrons → 1 mol H₂. So n(H₂) = n(e⁻) ÷ 2 = 0.01865 ÷ 2 = 0.009326 mol

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: n(H₂) = n(e⁻) / 2. Each H₂ molecule requires 2 electrons. So 0.01865 ÷ 2 = 0.009326 mol H₂.
error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Check the half equation: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂. The ratio of electrons to H₂ is 2:1 — divide moles of electrons by 2.

fields.label: Volume of H₂ at rtp = _____ dm³

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: At rtp, volume = moles × 24 dm³/mol. Multiply moles of H₂ by 24.
